answers.d01: 似然回答的是：假设某套参数为真，看到眼前这些数据的概率有多大。后验回答的是相反方向：看到数据之后，这套参数为真的概率有多大。例：某病患病率1%（先验），患者检测阳性率99%。似然是 P(阳性|患病)=0.99——先认定参数，算数据的概率；后验是 P(患病|阳性)——先看到数据，反推参数。把0.99直接当后验会严重高估：1000人中约10人患病，检出9.9个真阳性；990名健康人按5%假阳率贡献49.5个阳性，故后验≈9.9/59.4≈17%。贝叶斯公式就是两者间的换算器：后验 ∝ 似然×先验。先验越低，同样强的似然也拉不起后验——这就是它们的关系：似然是证据的强度，后验是结合起点后更新的信念。
answers.d02: Population variance answers: how spread out are the numbers around their average? Averages alone can mislead—{2,4,6,8} and {4,5,5,6} both average 5, but the first is clearly more scattered. Variance turns that into one number: take each value's distance from the mean, square it, then average those squared distances: σ² = (1/N)Σ(xᵢ−μ)². For {2,4,6,8} the deviations are −3,−1,1,3; squares 9,1,1,9; variance 20/4 = 5. The second set gives 0.5. Squaring exists so deviations do not cancel out (they would sum to zero) and so big outliers count extra; the price is units squared, which is why people often report the square root, the standard deviation, to get back to original units. Change one condition: multiply every value by 2 and each deviation doubles, so variance quadruples to 20—spread is very sensitive to scale.
answers.d03: 正反馈是输出的结果反过来加强输入，让变化自我放大。麦克风对准音箱：话筒拾到的声音经音箱放大，再被话筒拾到，一圈比一圈响，直到刺耳啸叫。机制是环形因果——A增强B，B又增强A，每绕一圈都在原方向上加码。房价是常见例子：涨价催生还会涨的预期，更多人买入，于是真的继续涨。但正反馈不等于好事：它只描述放大的方向，不评判结果。雪崩、银行挤兑、通货膨胀螺旋都是同一结构，把小扰动推成失控。与它对照的是负反馈——空调恒温，偏离目标就被拉回，系统因此稳定。所以分析一个系统先辨认反馈方向：遇到正反馈要问什么在给它踩刹车（利率、库存、监管），没有制动的放大，迟早以崩坏收场。
answers.d04: Opportunity cost is the value of the best option you give up when you choose one thing. You have a free afternoon: hike, nap, or study for tomorrow's quiz. You pick studying. The cost is not all skipped options combined—it is only the single best one you passed up, say the hike, if that is what you would have done next. The nap was never in contention. Notice the cost is not money—the afternoon was free—but the forgone benefit of the hike. Change one condition: if it rains, the hike drops out and your cost becomes the nap instead; the same choice now costs less. Transfer this: when a friend calls a concert free, ask what else that evening could have delivered. Every choice is priced in its best alternative, not in cash.
answers.d05: 阳性结果不等于患病，因为健康人远多于病人，假阳性会大量堆积。用贝叶斯公式算一遍。设患病率1%，灵敏度99%（病人99%显阳性），假阳性率5%。取1000人：约10人患病，其中9.9人检出阳性；990名健康人中5%即49.5人误报阳性。于是59.4个阳性里只有9.9个真病人：P(患病|阳性)=9.9/59.4≈17%。贝叶斯公式做的就是这件事：后验 = (先验×似然) ÷ 所有能产生该证据的概率之和，即 0.01×0.99 ÷ (0.01×0.99 + 0.99×0.05)。先验是检测前对患病率的判断，后验是拿到阳性后的更新值，似然描述检测本身的可靠度。条件变化：同样是这台机器，若用在患病率5%的高危人群，后验升到约51%——证据相同，起点不同，结论就不同。
answers.d06: Cache invalidation is the problem of keeping a fast copy from disagreeing with the slow source of truth. A web app caches the product price in memory: reads take 1 ms instead of a 50 ms database hit. When the price changes in the database, the cached copy is stale—users still see the old price. Invalidation is deciding when and how to drop or refresh that copy. Three common strategies: TTL (expire after 60 seconds—simple, but data can be stale for up to 60 s); delete-on-write (update the database, then remove the cache key so the next read repopulates it fresh); write-through (update cache and database together on every write). The hard part is scale: with many cache nodes and many writers, figuring out which copies are now wrong gets genuinely difficult—that is why people joke it is one of the two hard problems in computer science. Change one condition: if prices must never be wrong for even a second, TTL alone cannot deliver; you need write-time invalidation.
answers.d07: 相关只说明两个量一起变动，因果还要求一个量的变化由另一个引起。例：某城市冰淇淋月销量与溺水人数同涨同跌，相关很强，但禁售冰淇淋不会减少溺水——两者背后有共同的第三者：夏天气温高，这叫混杂因素。判断因果要看三点：有没有共同原因；方向会不会倒过来（是游泳的人顺路买冰淇淋，还是相反）；控制其他条件后相关是否仍在——只比较气温相近的月份，若相关消失，说明它只是气温制造的假象。换条件检验：冬天溺水几乎为零而冰淇淋照卖，相关断裂，混杂暴露。但相关并非永远不能当因果：吸烟与肺癌在排除了年龄、职业等混杂后相关依然成立，加上生物学机制，因果判断才站得住。相关是线索，因果要靠控制条件和机制证实。
answers.d08: Compound growth means growth on top of past growth: each period's gain is computed on the new total, not the original start. Formula: final = P(1+r)^t. Invest $1,000 at 10%: year 1 earns $100, but year 2 earns $110 because the interest itself earns interest; after 10 years you hold $2,594, not $2,000. The starting amount P matters because it multiplies the whole curve: at the same rate and years, $2,000 ends at $5,187—exactly double. But the t in the exponent is where compounding bites hardest: start 10 years earlier and the same $1,000 runs 20 years, ending near $6,727—more than triple the 10-year result. The earliest dollar is the most valuable one. Condition to watch: the rate also sits in the exponent; at 7%, money doubles roughly every decade (rule of 72), so a small rate change compounds into a large final gap.
answers.v01: 过拟合是模型把训练数据里的噪声也当成了规律。类比：一个学生把练习题答案全背下来，练习册满分，考试换道新题就不会——他记住的是题目本身，不是解法。模型也一样：参数太多、数据太少时，它能给每个训练样本定制一条曲线，把偶然的误差起伏也拟合进去。判断依据：训练误差很低，但在没见过的新数据上误差明显更高，这个落差就是过拟合的信号；反过来，若连训练数据都学不好，那是欠拟合，是规律没抓到。条件变化：增加数据量，偶然模式无法反复重现，模型难以硬背，过拟合减轻；或限制模型复杂度、加正则化，逼它放弃逐点记忆、去找更平缓的规律。所以评估模型永远看它在新数据上的表现，训练集分数说了不算。
answers.v02: Precision and recall measure two different failures of a search. You search jaguar and get 100 results, 80 of them about the animal and the rest about cars. Precision asks: of what we returned, how much was right? 80/100 = 80%. Recall asks: of everything that was right, how much did we return? If the library holds 400 relevant pages, recall is 80/400 = 20%. The two can trade off: return every page in the library and recall hits 100% while precision collapses; return only the single most certain hit and precision nears 100% while recall sinks. Which matters more depends on the cost of each error: a cancer screen must not miss cases (recall first), while a search drowning users in junk needs precision first. A combined single number, F1, takes the harmonic mean of the two, so it punishes lopsided results.
answers.v03: 自然选择不需要任何生物主动努力，它只是一个筛选过程。机制分三步：同种个体存在随机差异（有的鹿跑得快些）；差异可以遗传；差异影响存活和繁殖——跑得快的鹿更少被狼吃掉，留下更多后代。于是下一代种群中「快」基因的比例比上一代高。变化发生在种群的基因频率上，个体终生不变：一只慢鹿练习再久也不会变快，也没有鹿想要变快，只是跑得慢的个体留下后代的概率更小。长颈鹿的经典误读要纠正：不是祖先拼命伸脖子把脖子拉长，而是脖子稍长的个体在饥荒年份够得到高处叶片、活下来并繁殖，代代累积差异。条件变化：环境一变，筛选方向就变——狼消失后，跑得快的优势减弱，别的性状可能转而上升。
answers.v04: Idempotency means running the same operation many times leaves the same result as running it once. It matters in distributed systems because networks fail opaquely: you send a payment request, your timeout fires, but the server may have processed it—did the retry charge twice? With an idempotent design, no. The standard fix is a client-generated idempotency key per logical operation; the server stores the key with the result, and a retry with the same key returns the stored result instead of charging again. Compare methods: PUT /items/42 with the full body is naturally idempotent (same end state), while POST /increment is not (each call adds one). One caution: idempotency fixes the end state, not every side effect—retries may still send duplicate emails unless those are keyed too. Queues deliver at-least-once, so consumers must be idempotent to behave as exactly-once.
answers.v05: 信息熵衡量平均而言你有多难猜中结果，单位是比特。公式 H=−Σpᵢlog₂pᵢ：对每种可能，把它的概率 p 乘以 −log₂p，再求和。−log₂p 随概率升高趋于0，所以概率越大的结果出现时越不让人惊讶，熵就是平均惊讶量。均匀分布最不确定，原因在猜测者的处境：均匀硬币正面0.5，你只能瞎猜，错一半；偏置硬币正面0.9，你每次押正面，十次对九次，几乎不惊讶——可预测性高，熵低。均匀时所有选项同样可能，没有任何结果可押，熵达到最大值 log₂n：两个等可能选项是1比特，八个等可能选项是3比特。条件变化：把0.9/0.1拉平成0.5/0.5，熵从约0.47升到1——概率越接近均匀，结果越难预知。
answers.v06: Deadlock is when threads each hold a resource and wait forever for the other's, so none can proceed. Concrete allocation: thread T1 locks file A; thread T2 locks file B; T1 then requests B and blocks; T2 requests A and blocks. Each waits on the other, neither releases what it holds, both freeze. Four conditions must all hold: mutual exclusion (one owner per resource), hold-and-wait, no preemption (locks cannot be forcibly taken back), and circular wait. Break any one and deadlock becomes impossible—most systems break the circle with a global lock order: every thread must acquire A before B, so T2 can never hold B while waiting for A. Change one condition: give locks a timeout and T1 gives up and retries later—liveness returns, though repeated retry collisions (livelock) become possible. The same structure reappears with distributed locks and RPC chains, which is why ordering and timeouts matter there too.
answers.v07: 公共物品有两个特征：不付钱也拦不住你用（非排他），多一人用不减少别人可用（非竞争）。路灯、防洪堤、国防都如此。这带来搭便车问题：客厅装灯要花200元，四个室友每人受益150元。对个人来说，不出钱也能享受灯光，理性选择是等别人掏钱；结果四人都等，灯装不成——总收益600元明明超过成本200元。这就是市场失灵：钱收不上来，私人不愿供给，社会需要的东西反而缺货。改变条件：如果灯装了感应器、不交钱不亮（可排他），搭便车被堵住，市场就能供上。现实的解法也顺着这个思路：政府用税收强制集资修路灯、养国防，本质是消除不付钱也享用这条路。判断一件东西会不会供给不足，先问它能不能排他。
answers.v08: Little's law says L = λW: in a stable system, the average number of items inside (L) equals the arrival rate (λ) times the average time each spends in the system (W). Coffee-shop version: 10 customers arrive per minute and each stays 2 minutes from door to drink-in-hand, so on average 10 × 2 = 20 people are inside. The law is a counting identity, not a performance claim: it holds for any queue discipline and any arrival pattern, because everyone who enters eventually leaves, so inventory must equal inflow × residence time. It is useful diagnostically—measure any two quantities to get the third. If a server takes λ = 100 requests/sec with average latency W = 0.05 s, then L = 5 requests are in flight. Watch the stability condition: arrival rate must not exceed service capacity; if it does, the queue grows without bound and W stops being a fixed number, so the simple reading breaks.
